intro: Lesson 17: The boycott in the valley. To understand how the Prophet's ﷺ family and the Muslims stayed patient through the boycott

questions.q: Describe two hardships of the boycott.
questions.a: Not enough food; no trade; cut off from friends and family
questions.model: Teacher: First hardship: there was very little food, so children were hungry. Second: no one would trade or speak with them, so they felt alone.

questions.a: Banu Hashim, the Prophet's ﷺ clan
options: Banu Hashim, the Prophet's ﷺ clan

questions.q: About how long did it last?
In the portal response box, write a message of hope (from today, to the people in the valley). Start: 'Even though you are hungry and alone, ...'
questions.a: Mentions patience, trust in Allah, sharing, and that the hardship will end.
questions.model: Teacher writes: 'Even though you are hungry and alone, Allah sees your patience, and every hardship has an end.'

questions.q: why did some Makkans help secretly?
questions.a: They knew it was unfair and cared for their relatives.

questions.q: link to 94:5-6 'With hardship comes ease'. What does it promise?
questions.a: Hardship does not last for ever; ease comes with it.

questions.q: What was left on the eaten agreement?
Back to our ponder: how did they keep going?
questions.a: Patience, sharing and trust in Allah.
